title: Postdoctoral Fellowship in Health Economics
description:
Description

Dartmouth College invites applications for one postdoctoral fellow
at The Dartmouth Institute for Health Policy and Clinical Practice
at the Geisel School of Medicine. This fellowship will support a
scholar whose research improves the quality, accessibility, and
cost of health care. The fellow will work directly with the Health
Economics and Policy Lab and Drs. Carrie Colla, Emma Dean, and
Johnny Huynh. Specific areas of interest include, but are not
limited to, payment and delivery systems, rural health, the
pharmaceutical industry, primary care and emergency care, and
health care disparities.

This fellowship promotes student and faculty diversity at Dartmouth
and across higher education by supporting scholars who have
demonstrated a commitment to and ability to advance educational
diversity and inclusion. Applicants will be selected based on their
academic achievement, promise in research and teaching, and
potential to advance diversity and inclusion in higher
education.

This is a two-year residential fellowship. Fellows are expected to
pursue research and collaborate on grant writing while fully
participating in the department's and the college's intellectual
life. Fellows receive an annual stipend, benefits, and a research
expense allocation (exact funding levels will be determined at the
time of offer).

Dartmouth is committed to academic excellence and encourages the
open exchange of ideas within a culture of mutual respect. People
with different backgrounds, life experiences, and perspectives make
the Dartmouth community diverse, which enhances academic
excellence.

Qualifications

PhD in Economics, Health Policy, or a related field. Applicants
should have received a PhD or be on track to complete their PhD by
June 2027.

Application Instructions

Please submit the following application materials:


Job market paper.
Research statement outlining completed research (including job
market paper), work in progress, and plans for publication (maximum
three pages, single-spaced).
Teaching statement outlining past and future teaching interests
(maximum one page, single-spaced).
Fellowship program statement describing your motivation to join
a multidisciplinary cohort and how your research, teaching,
service, and/or life experiences prepare you to advance Dartmouth's
commitment to diversity in service of academic excellence (maximum
two pages).
Curriculum vitae, including the names and contact information
of three references.
Three confidential letters of recommendation, one of which
should be from the dissertation advisor.



Applications will be reviewed beginning January 12, 2027, and will
continue until the position is filled.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement

Dartmouth College is an equal opportunity employer under federal
law. We prohibit discrimination on the basis of race, color,
religion, sex, age, national origin, sexual orientation, gender
identity or expression, disability, veteran status, marital status,
or any other legally protected status. Applications are welcome
from all.

Dartmouth is committed to accessibility for its community. If you
are an applicant with a disability and would like to request a
reasonable accommodation to aid in the job application and/or
interview process, please email: ADA@Dartmouth.edu . In the subject
line, please state application accommodations and include the job
number or title. Someone from the ADA/504 Office will be in touch
within 2 business days.

For additional employment opportunities at Dartmouth College,
please visit the Dartmouth Interfolio
Job Board , the 
Office of the Provost , and the Office of Human Resources
.

Offers of employment are contingent upon consent to a
pre-employment background check with results acceptable under
Dartmouth 
policy . Please visit the Dartmouth policy portal for faculty
handbooks and details of other Dartmouth policies .
